newsitem.title: JAPAN: Victor Japan to set up joint venture in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Victor Japan to set up joint venture in Vietnam.

text.p: Victor Co of Japan said on Monday that it would set up a joint venture in Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City towards the end of January to manufacture and sell its audio-visual products.

The joint venture, JVC Vietnam Ltd, will be capitalised at $3 million. Victor will own 70 percent of the firm, while state-run Viettronics Tan Binh Co is to hold the remainder, Victor said in a statement.
The joint venture is expected to start producing televisions, video players and audio equipment in March. Its initial production capacity will be 100,000 units per year, the statement said.
The company plans to quadruple capacity in five years, it said.
Victor has been supplying parts for televisions to the joint venture partner.
Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd announced last October that it was setting up a joint venture in Vietnam with Viettronics Thu Duc Co to produce audio-visual equipment.

Toshiba Corp, one of Matsushita's competitors in the consumer electronics business, also said in October that it had set up a joint venture in Vietnam with Viettronics Thu Duc to produce and sell colour television sets.
